Both fixes are in, with all 302 web tests passing and typecheck clean.

**OAuth fix** — The web app's "Sign in with Anthropic" was failing at the token-exchange step. The server handlers (`web/server/api/oauth/token.ts` and `refresh.ts`) were posting `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies to `platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token`, but Anthropic's endpoint only accepts JSON — I confirmed this against the pi-ai OAuth implementation the CLI uses (which works and posts JSON). Both the initial code exchange and token refresh now send JSON for Anthropic while keeping form encoding for OpenAI Codex and Google, which expect it. I also added `code=true` to the Anthropic authorize URL (`web/src/keating/oauth.ts:44`) — that's the parameter that makes Anthropic's callback page actually display the `code#state` string you paste back into the app; reference implementations all include it. Added a regression test for it in `oauth.test.ts`.

**Intro fix** — In `web/src/pages/Chat.tsx` the dismissal was stored in `sessionStorage`, so every new tab or browser restart showed the intro again. It now writes to `localStorage` (once per user per browser), still honors an old `sessionStorage` flag, and — per your point about session data — a new effect checks saved sessions on load: if any exist, the intro is skipped and marked dismissed automatically, so returning users land directly in the chat.

One caveat: if the OAuth trouble you were seeing was with the Google or OpenAI popup flows rather than Anthropic, that's a different failure mode — those use your site origin as the redirect URI, which has to be registered with the provider's OAuth client — so let me know and I'll dig into that path instead.

---
name: oauth-providers
description: >-
  Debug OAuth sign-in failures and add new OAuth providers to Keating (web +

# OAuth providers in Keating

How OAuth sign-in works in this repo, the provider-specific quirks that have
already caused bugs, and the checklist for adding a new provider.

## Architecture

The web app uses an authorization-code + PKCE flow, brokered through the
Nitro server so tokens are exchanged server-side:

| Piece | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Provider registry | `web/src/keating/oauth.ts` (`OAUTH_PROVIDERS`) | Client IDs, authorize/token URLs, scopes, redirect URIs, extra authorize params |
| Redirect resolution | `web/src/keating/oauth.ts` (`resolveOAuthRedirectUri`) | Prod (`keating.help`) → `https://keating.help/oauth/callback`; everywhere else → the provider's CLI loopback URI + manual paste |
| Popup + pending state | `web/src/keating/oauth.ts` (`initiateOAuth`) | Saves `{verifier, state, redirectUri}` to localStorage under `keating_oauth_pending`, opens the authorize popup |
| Callback page | `web/src/pages/OAuthCallback.tsx` (route `/oauth/callback`) | Runs `completeOAuthFromInput(location.href)`, posts `keating-oauth-result` message to the opener |
| Manual paste input | `web/src/components/settings/CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx` | Shown while sign-in is pending; accepts a pasted callback URL, `code#state`, query string, or bare code |
| Token exchange | `web/server/api/oauth/token.ts` | POSTs to the provider's token URL with the stored verifier |
| Token refresh | `web/server/api/oauth/refresh.ts` | Auto-refresh 60s before expiry; 401/403 deletes stored credentials |
| Server client config | `web/server/api/oauth/config.ts` | Client IDs/secrets, env-overridable (`OAUTH_<PROVIDER>_CLIENT_ID` / `_SECRET`) |
| Consumption | `web/src/lib/provider-models.ts` (`getProviderApiKey`) | OAuth token (or exchanged API key) wins over stored API keys |
| Reference implementation | `web/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/utils/oauth/*.js` | The CLI's working flows — **check here first when a web flow misbehaves** |

Credentials are stored per provider as JSON under the `oauth:<id>` key in
`getAppStorage().providerKeys`. Provider-name aliasing (`openai` →
`openai-codex`, `google` → `google-gemini-cli`) lives in `providerToOAuthId`.

After editing `web/src/keating/oauth.ts`, regenerate the sandbox snapshot:
`bun scripts/generate-nodepod-boot-files.ts`.

## Provider quirks (hard-won; do not regress)

**Anthropic** (client `9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e`, Claude Pro/Max):
- The token endpoint `https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` only accepts
  **JSON bodies** (`Content-Type: application/json`), for both code exchange
  and refresh. Form-urlencoded fails. This is special-cased in `token.ts` and
  `refresh.ts`.
- Uses the provider-hosted code-display callback
  (`https://platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback`) in **all** environments;
  the user copies a `code#state` string. `code=true` must be in the authorize
  params or the code is never displayed.
- `state` must equal the PKCE **verifier** (not a random value), and must be
  sent in the token exchange body.
- Resulting `sk-ant-oat-*` access tokens are handled downstream by pi-ai
  (Bearer + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` headers) — pass them through as
  the "apiKey"; do not put them in `x-api-key` yourself.

**OpenAI Codex** (client `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann`, ChatGPT Plus/Pro):
- Only `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback` is registered; any web-origin
  redirect is rejected at the authorize step (unless keating.help is registered
  on the client used — see redirect resolution above).
- Form-urlencoded token exchange is correct here.
- After exchange, the `id_token` is swapped for a real OpenAI API key via a
  token-exchange grant (`web/server/api/oauth/openai-codex.ts`,
  `requested_token: openai-api-key`).
- Authorize needs `id_token_add_organizations=true`,
  `codex_cli_simplified_flow=true`, `originator`.

**Google Gemini CLI** (client `681255809395-oo8f…`, installed app):
- Installed-app clients accept **any localhost port** as redirect but **no
  https origins**, and the token exchange **requires the client secret** —
  the Gemini CLI's secret is public by design (embedded in its open-source
  repo; Google docs say installed-app secrets are not confidential) and is the
  fallback in `web/server/api/oauth/config.ts`.
- Authorize needs `access_type=offline&prompt=consent` or no refresh token is
  returned.

## Debugging a failing sign-in

1. Reproduce and note **which step** fails:
   - Error on the provider's authorize page → redirect URI not registered for
     that client, or missing required authorize params.
   - "Token exchange failed: 502 …" from the app → server-side exchange
     rejected; check the Nitro log line `[oauth/token] <provider> token
     exchange failed: <status> <body>` for the upstream error.
   - Signed in but requests 401 → token consumed incorrectly (see quirks), or
     refresh failing (`[oauth/refresh]` log).
2. Diff the failing flow against the CLI's pi-ai implementation
   (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/utils/oauth/`) — encoding (JSON
   vs form), authorize params, state semantics, redirect URI. Every web bug so
   far has been a divergence from those reference flows.
3. Fix in the smallest layer (registry vs server handler), then run
   `cd web && bun test src/test/oauth.test.ts && bunx tsc --noEmit`.

## Adding a new provider

1. Add the entry to `OAUTH_PROVIDERS` in `web/src/keating/oauth.ts` (extend
   `OAuthProviderId`). Set `redirectUri` if the client only accepts a fixed

# OAuth providers in Keating

How OAuth sign-in works in this repo, the provider-specific quirks that have
already caused bugs, and the checklist for adding a new provider.

## Architecture

The web app uses an authorization-code + PKCE flow, brokered through the
Nitro server so tokens are exchanged server-side:

| Piece | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Provider registry | `web/src/keating/oauth.ts` (`OAUTH_PROVIDERS`) | Client IDs, authorize/token URLs, scopes, redirect URIs, extra authorize params |
| Redirect resolution | `web/src/keating/oauth.ts` (`resolveOAuthRedirectUri`) | Prod (`keating.help`) → `https://keating.help/oauth/callback`; everywhere else → the provider's CLI loopback URI + manual paste |
| Popup + pending state | `web/src/keating/oauth.ts` (`initiateOAuth`) | Saves `{verifier, state, redirectUri}` to localStorage under `keating_oauth_pending`, opens the authorize popup |
| Callback page | `web/src/pages/OAuthCallback.tsx` (route `/oauth/callback`) | Runs `completeOAuthFromInput(location.href)`, posts `keating-oauth-result` message to the opener |
| Manual paste input | `web/src/components/settings/CloudProviderKeysSection.tsx` | Shown while sign-in is pending; accepts a pasted callback URL, `code#state`, query string, or bare code |
| Token exchange | `web/server/api/oauth/token.ts` | POSTs to the provider's token URL with the stored verifier |
| Token refresh | `web/server/api/oauth/refresh.ts` | Auto-refresh 60s before expiry; 401/403 deletes stored credentials |
| Server client config | `web/server/api/oauth/config.ts` | Client IDs/secrets, env-overridable (`OAUTH_<PROVIDER>_CLIENT_ID` / `_SECRET`) |
| Consumption | `web/src/lib/provider-models.ts` (`getProviderApiKey`) | OAuth token (or exchanged API key) wins over stored API keys |
| Reference implementation | `web/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/utils/oauth/*.js` | The CLI's working flows — **check here first when a web flow misbehaves** |

Credentials are stored per provider as JSON under the `oauth:<id>` key in
`getAppStorage().providerKeys`. Provider-name aliasing (`openai` →
`openai-codex`, `google` → `google-gemini-cli`) lives in `providerToOAuthId`.

After editing `web/src/keating/oauth.ts`, regenerate the sandbox snapshot:
`bun scripts/generate-nodepod-boot-files.ts`.

## Provider quirks (hard-won; do not regress)

**Anthropic** (client `9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e`, Claude Pro/Max):
- The token endpoint `https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token` only accepts
  **JSON bodies** (`Content-Type: application/json`), for both code exchange
  and refresh. Form-urlencoded fails. This is special-cased in `token.ts` and
  `refresh.ts`.
- Uses the provider-hosted code-display callback
  (`https://platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback`) in **all** environments;
  the user copies a `code#state` string. `code=true` must be in the authorize
  params or the code is never displayed.
- `state` must equal the PKCE **verifier** (not a random value), and must be
  sent in the token exchange body.
- Resulting `sk-ant-oat-*` access tokens are handled downstream by pi-ai
  (Bearer + `anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20` headers) — pass them through as
  the "apiKey"; do not put them in `x-api-key` yourself.

**OpenAI Codex** (client `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann`, ChatGPT Plus/Pro):
- Only `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback` is registered; any web-origin
  redirect is rejected at the authorize step (unless keating.help is registered
  on the client used — see redirect resolution above).
- Form-urlencoded token exchange is correct here.
- After exchange, the `id_token` is swapped for a real OpenAI API key via a
  token-exchange grant (`web/server/api/oauth/openai-codex.ts`,
  `requested_token: openai-api-key`).
- Authorize needs `id_token_add_organizations=true`,
  `codex_cli_simplified_flow=true`, `originator`.

**Google Gemini CLI** (client `681255809395-oo8f…`, installed app):
- Installed-app clients accept **any localhost port** as redirect but **no
  https origins**, and the token exchange **requires the client secret** —
  the Gemini CLI's secret is public by design (embedded in its open-source
  repo; Google docs say installed-app secrets are not confidential) and is the
  fallback in `web/server/api/oauth/config.ts`.
- Authorize needs `access_type=offline&prompt=consent` or no refresh token is
  returned.

## Debugging a failing sign-in

1. Reproduce and note **which step** fails:
   - Error on the provider's authorize page → redirect URI not registered for
     that client, or missing required authorize params.
   - "Token exchange failed: 502 …" from the app → server-side exchange
     rejected; check the Nitro log line `[oauth/token] <provider> token
     exchange failed: <status> <body>` for the upstream error.
   - Signed in but requests 401 → token consumed incorrectly (see quirks), or
     refresh failing (`[oauth/refresh]` log).

5. Tests in `web/src/test/oauth.test.ts`: provider wiring, redirect URI

**Reference files:** `web/src/pages/Terms.tsx` (cleanest example), `web/src/pages/Download.tsx`, `web/src/components/Nav.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`

```tsx
import { Nav } from "../components/Nav";
import { Footer } from "../components/Footer";
import { useSeo } from "../hooks/useSeo";

export function Pricing() {
  useSeo({
    title: "Pricing | Keating",
    description: "...",
    canonical: "https://keating.help/pricing",
  });
  return (
    <div className="retro-layout retro-page">   {/* Download uses these; Terms adds "legal-layout" */}
      <Nav />
      <main> ... </main>
      <Footer />
    </div>
  );
}
```
Note: the page component is a **named export** (`export function Terms()` / `export function Download()`), because App.tsx imports it by name via `lazyRouteComponent(..., "Terms")`.

### Retro styling conventions
- Layout wrappers: `retro-layout retro-page` (Download.tsx:~top-level div); legal pages add `legal-layout` / `legal-page` / `legal-doc paper-fold distressed-border` (Terms.tsx:19-22).

- Section eyebrow header uses a terminal prompt: `<div className="eyebrow prompt">cat TERMS_OF_SERVICE.txt</div>` (Terms.tsx:23). Download uses `<div className="eyebrow prompt">tail -f MOBILE_ROADMAP</div>`.

- `useSeo` hook: `web/src/hooks/useSeo.ts`, takes `{ title, description, canonical }`.

### Registering a new route (App.tsx) — exact pattern
Three edits, mirroring `downloadRoute`/`termsRoute`:

1. Lazy component declaration (App.tsx:38-45 region):
```tsx
const Pricing = lazyRouteComponent(
  () => loadRouteChunk(() => import("./pages/Pricing")),
  "Pricing",
);
```

```tsx
  getParentRoute: () => rootRoute,
  path: "/pricing",
  component: Pricing,

```

```tsx
const routeTree = rootRoute.addChildren([
  ...,
  downloadRoute,
  termsRoute,
```

- Desktop list, inside `<div className="nav-desktop">` (Nav.tsx ~lines 90-110), pattern:

```tsx
<Link to="/pricing" className="nav-link glitch-hover font-terminal nav-desktop-link">
  [PRICING]
```

```tsx

  [PRICING]
</Link>
```

## 2. Existing Dio purchase UX (reusable)

**Files:** `web/src/components/DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`, `web/src/pages/DioSuccess.tsx`

`DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx` is a modal (styled with Tailwind/shadcn tokens — `bg-background`, `text-muted-foreground`, `btn` via className — NOT retro styling) driven by a module-level singleton + custom events (`promptDioAccess()` returns a Promise<boolean>, `closeDioPrompt(success)`, `getActiveDioPrompt()`). It has three `mode`s and these state flows:

- **purchase mode** (`doCheckout`, DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx:105-122): validates email → `startDioCheckout(normalized)` → stores `result.purchaseReference` → `window.open(result.checkoutUrl, "_blank")`. After returning, a "Claim" button appears calling `doClaim`.
- **claim** (`doClaim`, lines 124-149): `claimDioAccess(normalized, purchaseReference)` → on `result.success && result.apiKey`: `getAppStorage().providerKeys.set(DIO_PROVIDER_ID, apiKey)` + `rememberDioIdentity(normalized)` + close. Handles `result.pending` ("still pending") and not-found.
- **recover mode** (`doRecover`, lines 151-179): `recoverDioAccess(normalized, otp)` → OTP email flow; sets `requiresOtp`, surfaces `result.devCode` in dev. On success same key-store + remember pattern.
- **manual mode** (`saveManualKey`, lines 88-103): paste a Bifrost virtual key directly into `providerKeys`.

`DioSuccess.tsx` (page at `/dio/success`) is the **post-checkout return landing**. Reads `dio_ref` + `dio_email` from URL query, then `claimDioAccess(normalized, ref)` with states `"claiming" | "success" | "error"`. On success: store key, `rememberDioIdentity`, PostHog `identify` + `capture('dio_access_claimed')`, redirect to `/chat` after 1200ms. No polling loop — it's a single claim attempt; `pending` → tells user to refresh.

### Functions to reuse (from `web/src/dio-provider/index.ts`)
Exports (index.ts:55-152):
- `startDioCheckout(email)` → `{ checkoutUrl, purchaseReference }` (index.ts:85)
- `claimDioAccess(email, purchaseReference?)` → `{ success, apiKey?, pending?, error? }` (index.ts:98)
- `recoverDioAccess(email, otp?)` → `{ success, apiKey?, requiresOtp?, devCode? }` (index.ts:111)
- `normalizeEmail(email)` (index.ts:124), `rememberDioIdentity(email)` (index.ts:65), `getStoredDioIdentity()` (index.ts:73), `getDioAccessStatus()` (index.ts:55), `isDioFeatureEnabled()` (index.ts:152)
- Constants: `DIO_PROVIDER_ID = "dio"`, `DIO_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID = "kimi-k2.6"`, `DIO_DEFAULT_MODEL` (index.ts:3-24)

For a /pricing page, the simplest reuse is to call `promptDioAccess()` (from DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx) on a "Buy" button, or call `startDioCheckout` directly and redirect.

## 3. Webhook budget/product handling

**Files:** `web/server/api/dio/webhook.ts`, `web/server/api/dio/claim.ts`, config in `web/src/dio-provider/server.ts`

### Where `budget.max` comes from
`createBifrostVirtualKey(config, { ..., budget: { max: config.dioCreditBudget }, ... })` — **webhook.ts:140**.

`config.dioCreditBudget` is loaded in `getDioEnvConfig()` at **server.ts:40**:
```ts
const dioCreditBudget = Number.parseInt(getRequiredEnv("DIO_CREDIT_BUDGET"), 10);
// validated >0 at server.ts:44-45
```
So the budget is a **single global env-driven constant** — one flat value applied to every purchase regardless of pack.

### Product identification (critical for multiple pack sizes)
The webhook resolves a product id and **rejects anything that isn't the one configured product** (webhook.ts:48-52):
```ts
const productId = object?.order?.product || object?.product?.id;
if (productId !== config.creemProductId) {   // config.creemProductId = env CREEM_PRODUCT_ID_DIO_CREDITS (server.ts:39)
  throw createError({ statusCode: 400, statusMessage: "Product ID mismatch" });
}
```
The `productId` **is** captured (stored on the entitlement and in the Bifrost key metadata: `creemProductId: productId`, webhook.ts:~152), but budget does **not** vary by it. To support multiple pack sizes you'd need to:
- allow a set of product ids (replace the single `!==` check), and
- map each product id → a budget (e.g., a `Record<productId, budget>` instead of the single `dioCreditBudget`), passing the mapped value into `budget: { max }`.

Checkout is single-product too: `product_id: config.creemProductId` at server.ts:127.

### Repeat purchases: top-up vs new key
**Neither — repeat purchases by the same email are ignored (idempotent by email), no top-up.** webhook.ts:73-79:
```ts
const existing = await loadDioEntitlement(storage, email);
if (existing) {
  await completeEvent(storage, payload.id, true);
  return { ... entitlement: { email, virtualKeyId: existing.virtualKeyId } };  // returns existing key, no budget increase
}
```
There is also idempotency by `purchaseReference` (provisioning records, webhook.ts:88-125) and a per-event lock (`acquireEventLock`, webhook.ts:~60). So a second purchase on the same email creates **no** new key and does **not** add credits — the existing key is simply returned. Supporting top-ups (increasing `budget.max` on the existing Bifrost key) would be new logic.

`claim.ts`: returns `entitlement.virtualKeyValue` only when the posted `purchaseReference` matches the stored one (claim.ts:38-40); otherwise `pending`/not-found. One entitlement per email.

## 4. Existing token/pricing display

- **Cost formatting:** `web/src/pages/Usage.tsx:24-25`:
  ```ts
  function formatCost(value: number) {
    return value > 0 ? `$${value.toFixed(value < 1 ? 4 : 2)}` : "$0";
  }
  ```
  Costs are pre-aggregated per session as `session.usage.cost.total` (Usage.tsx:438; also `web/src/components/usage-chart-data.ts:100`). Displayed via the stat-tile at Usage.tsx:494 (`value={formatCost(totals.cost)}`).
- **`usage-topic-groups.ts`** is actually at `web/src/components/usage-topic-groups.ts` (not in `keating/`). It handles **topic categorization/hierarchy only** (`categorizeUsageTopic`, `buildTopicArtifactGroups`) — no token or cost formatting. Not useful for pricing.
- **Model cost-per-token constants:** the app has a cost shape `{ input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite }` but **all values are currently 0** — there is no real per-token price table:
  - `web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:38-45` `modelCost()` returns all zeros.
  - `web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:404-409` `UNKNOWN_COST` is all zeros (used for saved/custom models including Dio, lines 426, 478).

  So displayed `cost.total` is effectively 0 for Dio models today; **there is no existing constant defining Dio/Kimi per-token pricing.** A transparent pay-per-token /pricing page would need to introduce those numbers (either hard-coded on the page or by populating `modelCost()`/a new pricing constant). The cost struct shape to match is `{ input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite }` (per-token USD).

### Summary of exact patterns
- **Add route:** 3 edits in `web/src/App.tsx` — `lazyRouteComponent` decl, `createRoute({ path: "/pricing", component: Pricing })`, add to `rootRoute.addChildren([...])`. Page must be a named export `export function Pricing()`.
- **Add nav link:** 2 edits in `web/src/components/Nav.tsx` (desktop `nav-desktop` list + mobile `#mobile-menu` list), class `nav-link glitch-hover font-terminal nav-desktop-link`, label `[PRICING]`.
- **Page shell:** `retro-layout retro-page` + `<Nav/>`/`<Footer/>` + `useSeo`, retro classes `wrap`, `eyebrow prompt`, `btn-retro`, `desktop-download-card` (for pack cards), `font-terminal`.
- **Purchase reuse:** `startDioCheckout(email)` / `promptDioAccess()` from the dio-provider; success lands on existing `/dio/success` (`DioSuccess.tsx`).
- **Webhook budget:** single global `DIO_CREDIT_BUDGET` env → `budget.max`; product locked to one `CREEM_PRODUCT_ID_DIO_CREDITS`; repeat same-email purchases are ignored (idempotent, no top-up). Multi-pack support requires code changes in both `server.ts` (config/checkout) and `webhook.ts` (product→budget mapping + top-up logic).</result>

- **Scope**: full public `/pricing` route (pack cards, rate table, FAQ), buy buttons drive the existing Dio checkout; nav link added.

# Pricing page for Dio inference (token packs + transparent pay-per-token)

## Context

Keating sells hosted inference ("Dio" provider, Kimi K2.6 via a Bifrost gateway) but has no pricing page: a single Creem product is bought through an in-app dialog (`DioAccessPromptDialog`), and every purchase provisions a Bifrost virtual key with one global dollar budget (`DIO_CREDIT_BUDGET`). The user wants a public `/pricing` page selling multiple credit packs with transparent pay-per-token rates.

Decisions made with the user:
- **Packs**: $10 / $25 / $50, each its own Creem product.
- **Advertised rates (Kimi K2.6)**: $1 per M input tokens, $4 per M output tokens. Credits draw down at these rates.
- **Scope**: full public `/pricing` route (pack cards, rate table, FAQ), buy buttons drive the existing Dio checkout; nav link added.

Critical backend gap found in exploration: the webhook (`web/server/api/dio/webhook.ts`) rejects any product ID other than the single configured one, and **ignores repeat purchases by the same email** (returns the existing key, adds no credits). Selling packs requires multi-product support and top-ups.

## Plan

### 1. Shared pack catalog — new `web/src/dio-provider/packs.ts`

Dependency-free module used by both the Vite client and Nitro server (same pattern as the rest of `web/src/dio-provider/`):

- `DIO_TOKEN_RATES = { inputPerMTok: 1, outputPerMTok: 4 }` (advertised USD).
- `DIO_PACKS`: `[{ id: "starter", priceUsd: 10 }, { id: "plus", priceUsd: 25, popular: true }, { id: "pro", priceUsd: 50 }]` with labels/blurbs and a helper computing "up to N M tokens" ranges from the rates (e.g. $10 ≈ 10M input / 2.5M output tokens).
- `DEFAULT_DIO_PACK_ID = "starter"`.

### 2. Server: multi-product checkout + per-pack budgets + top-ups

`web/src/dio-provider/server.ts`:
- Replace single `creemProductId`/`dioCreditBudget` in `DioEnvConfig` with `packs: Record<packId, { productId, budget }>` built from env: `CREEM_PRODUCT_ID_DIO_PACK_STARTER|PLUS|PRO` and `DIO_PACK_BUDGET_STARTER|PLUS|PRO` (budget defaults to the pack's `priceUsd`). Back-compat: `CREEM_PRODUCT_ID_DIO_CREDITS` + `DIO_CREDIT_BUDGET` map to the starter pack when the new vars are unset, so current deployments keep working.
- `createCreemCheckout(config, email, packId)` uses the pack's product id and includes `dio_pack_id` in checkout metadata.
- New `updateBifrostVirtualKeyBudget(config, keyId, newMax)` calling Bifrost's governance virtual-key update endpoint (`PUT /api/governance/virtual-keys/:id`), mirroring `createBifrostVirtualKey`'s error handling.

`web/server/api/dio/checkout.ts`: accept optional `packId` in the body (default `starter`, 400 on unknown), pass to `createCreemCheckout`, store `packId` on the pending record.

`web/server/api/dio/webhook.ts`:
- Resolve `productId` → pack via the config map (400 only if it matches no configured pack).
- Provision the virtual key with that pack's budget.
- **Top-up path**: when an entitlement already exists for the email, call `updateBifrostVirtualKeyBudget(existing.virtualKeyId, previousBudget + pack.budget)` instead of ignoring the purchase; track the running budget on the entitlement (`budgetMax` field) and update the provisioning record so `/dio/success` → `claimDioAccess` succeeds and returns the same key.

### 3. Client: pricing page + wiring

- New `web/src/pages/Pricing.tsx` (named export `Pricing`), shell per repo convention: `retro-layout retro-page`, `<Nav/>`, `<Footer/>`, `useSeo({title, description, canonical: "https://keating.help/pricing"})`, `eyebrow prompt` header (e.g. `cat PRICING.txt`). Content:
  - Rate table: $1/M input, $4/M output for Kimi K2.6 from `DIO_TOKEN_RATES` — "pay per token, credits never expire, no subscription".
  - Three pack cards reusing the `desktop-download-card` / `is-recommended` pattern (`web/src/pages/Download.tsx`) with `btn-retro` buy buttons showing price and ~token volume.
  - Short FAQ (how credits work, top-ups stack on one key, recovery by email, BYO-API-keys remain free).
- Buy button → `promptDioAccess({ packId })`: extend the existing dialog singleton (`web/src/components/DioAccessPromptDialog.tsx`) to accept an optional `packId`, and thread it through `startDioCheckout(email, packId)` in `web/src/dio-provider/index.ts` (defaults keep current in-app behavior). PostHog capture `pricing_pack_selected`.
- Route: 3 edits in `web/src/App.tsx` (`lazyRouteComponent` decl, `createRoute({ path: "/pricing" })`, add to `rootRoute.addChildren`). Nav: add `[PRICING]` to both hard-coded lists in `web/src/components/Nav.tsx` (desktop `nav-desktop` + mobile `#mobile-menu`).
- Transparent in-app costs: set `DIO_DEFAULT_MODEL.cost` in `web/src/dio-provider/index.ts` to the advertised rates (match pi-ai's cost-unit convention used by `modelCost()` in `web/src/lib/provider-models.ts` — verify per-token vs per-Mtok before setting) so the Usage page reports real spend for Dio.

### 4. Tests & regeneration

- Extend the existing dio server tests (in `web/src/test/`) covering: env→pack config mapping incl. legacy fallback, checkout pack validation, webhook product→budget selection, and the top-up path (mocked Bifrost update).
- Regenerate `web/src/keating/nodepod-boot-files.ts` (`bun scripts/generate-nodepod-boot-files.ts`) since `web/src/dio-provider/*` is snapshotted.

### Out of scope / notes

- Creem products for $25 and $50 must be created in the Creem dashboard and their IDs set in env — code reads them from env and hides packs whose product ID is missing (page still renders them but buy shows "unavailable" outside dev).
- Bifrost must have the $1/$4 model pricing configured gateway-side for drawdown to match the advertised rates; our budget math assumes it.
- If Bifrost's update endpoint differs from `PUT /api/governance/virtual-keys/:id`, adjust during implementation (verify against the deployed Bifrost's API; creation endpoint already in use is `POST /api/governance/virtual-keys`).

## Verification

1. `cd web && bun test && bunx tsc --noEmit` — all suites green including new pack/webhook tests.
2. `bun run dev` (web): visit `/pricing` — rate table, three packs, nav link on desktop + mobile; buy opens the email dialog and hits `/api/dio/checkout` with the right `packId` (observe network tab; Creem env unset locally → expect clean error surface).
3. Simulate webhook locally (POST signed payload with each product id) → storage shows per-pack budget; second purchase same email → Bifrost update called with summed budget (mock/log).
4. Verify `/dio/success` claim still returns a key after both first purchase and top-up.
